nodes.question: What types of rules influence interactions between actors?
nodes.answer: Interactions between actors are influenced by formal rules (such as laws, property rights, and policies) and informal rules (such as customs and norms).
nodes.paragraph: 2006 ; Duguma et al. 2014 ; Villamayor-Tomas et al. 2015 ; Runhaar et al. 2018 ). North ( 1991 p. 97) de nes institutions as humanly devised constraints that structure political, economic and socialinteraction. Such interaction between actors is based on formal rules (laws, property rights, policies, and so forth) and informal rules (customs, norms, and so forth) (Ostrom2006 ; Grundmann and Ehlers 2016 ; Spijkerboer et al. 2019 ). In this study, we aim to understand these rules as this allows us to nd out what prevents actors from different sectors from ful Iling integrative potential. The IAD framework by Ostrom ( 2011 ) is a renowned instrument for conducting systematic institutional analysis.It was initially developed in the 1980s as an attempt to structure the elements, categories of factors, and logical interconnections that explain how institutions work(McGinnis 2011a ). Since then, it has evolved signi cantly as well as extended in the form of other frameworks (e.g., the Social-Ecological System (SES) Framework byMcGinnis and Ostrom 2014 ).

nodes.question: Why is it important to go beyond rules on paper or institutional design in governance?
nodes.answer: It is important to address governance elements in action and interactions of actors rather than just relying on formal rules and structures.
nodes.paragraph: Three key elements of governance can be derived from this de nition: (a) actors, (b) processes, and (c) structures. The word use highlights the understanding of governance as a phenomenon that is constituted by the actions and interactions of actors (Bryson et al. 2015 ). Consequently, addressing these elements must go beyond rules on paper or institutional design (Bartley 2022 : 189).
